entry.title: Raspberry Pi WiFi Router with RaspAP: Step-by-Step Setup Guide
entry.summary:
Using a Raspberry Pi as a Wi-Fi router is a neat way to learn networking while building something actually useful. With RaspAP, most of the heavy lifting is handled through a clean web interface, so you don’t need to dive deep into Linux networking commands. lets dive into how to make Raspberry Pi into a WiFi Router with RaspAP RaspAP (Raspberry Pi Access Point) is an open-source tool that helps you turn a Raspberry Pi into a Wi-Fi access point or router. It manages services like hostapd, dnsmasq, and firewall rules behind the scenes and exposes everything through a browser-based dashboard. Raspberry Pi (Pi 3 / 4 / Zero W) microSD card (8GB or more) Raspberry Pi OS Internet connection (Ethernet or Wi-Fi) Download the pre-built RaspAP image from GitHub. Flash it to a 16GB microSD using Raspberry Pi Imager (Use custom image). Boot your Raspberry Pi and connect to the auto-created RaspAP Wi-Fi (password: ChangeMe). Open http://10.3.141.1
Login: admin / secret
A router-like dashboard shows clients, bandwidth, and hotspot controls.
Step 3: Customize Hotspot Settings
Change SSID and set a strong WPA2 password Pick a less crowded Wi-Fi channel Set the correct country code Reboot to apply changes Dashboard → Ad Blocking Enable blocklists and choose a provider Save and reboot That’s it. Your Raspberry Pi now works as a Wi-Fi router with network-wide ad blocking, filtering ads, trackers, and malicious domains for every connected device. Portable travel router Dedicated IoT network Learning Linux networking Custom hotspot with firewall control It’s flexible, lightweight, and surprisingly capable for such a small board. RaspAP makes it easy to turn a Raspberry Pi WiFi Router with RaspAP without complicated configuration. It’s a solid project for anyone who wants hands-on networking experience while building something practical with everyday hardware.
